title: Every steady what-if runs reference_day's thermostat simulation on the event loop: 384-960 simulate_step per call
claim: async_simulate(steady=True) calls whatif.schedule_days -> HeatPumpOptimizer.reference_day for both sides synchronously on the event loop thread, so each steady what-if (the card's simulate_plan, the fuse advisor, the cap tile) makes 384-960 ThermalModel.simulate_step calls on the loop and blocks it for 7.5-23.9 ms of host CPU (37-120 ms on a Pi at F=5), over B2's 100 ms when the ask sets a weekend comfort level.
mechanism: coordinator.py async_simulate: days = whatif.schedule_days(_scratch({})[:2], (scratch, inputs)) if steady; schedule_days evaluates o.reference_day(i) for the live and the what-if optimizer, which for each distinct day type of the week runs _build_comfort_bounds and two _compute_baseline_power passes (simulate_step per step) -- in the coroutine, between the two awaits, never through _await_off_loop. The same function's solves go to the process worker; this model work does not (bug class P10).

evidence.unit: ThermalModel.simulate_step calls on the loop thread per weekend-comfort what-if (384 in the other five steady cells); loop CPU inside schedule_days 23.9 ms host (median of 3)
evidence.machine: box B1 container (4 vCPU, shared by three seats), CPython 3.14, OpenBLAS pinned to 1 thread; solves on the shipped process-worker route
evidence.contention_note: call counts exact; the CPU (7.5-23.9 ms host; 0.81 reference solves for the weekend cell against B2's 0.675 = 100 ms/(F x 29.6 ms)) and the heartbeat gaps (up to 39.7 ms host) were taken at load1 5.4-6.0 and are provisional
evidence.tolerance: exact (count); CPU ±30 % (two runs: weekend 23.4 and 23.9 ms)

instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model:ThermalModel.simulate_step (calls on the loop thread) and heatpump_optimizer.whatif:schedule_days (loop thread CPU), driven through heatpump_optimizer.coordinator:HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator.async_simulate

perturbation.change: whatif.schedule_days replaced by a twin whose two reference_day evaluations run through coordinator._await_off_loop (the process worker) before the call, in memory
perturbation.observed_value: loop simulate_step 384 -> 0 (card_target) and 960 -> 0 (card_weekend); loop CPU in schedule_days -> 0; heartbeat gap 21.1 -> 11.3 ms and 39.7 -> 8.3 ms. Second lever: weekend comfort set (more distinct day types) moves the count UP 384 -> 960

metric_definition: simulate_step calls and thread CPU on the asyncio loop's thread during one async_simulate(steady=True), solves on the process worker.
phenomenon_property: No model kernel (simulate_step, simulate_trajectory*, a baseline-thermostat walk) runs on the event loop thread; a what-if's every model evaluation goes through the process worker as its solves do.
seam_rule: grep -n 'reference_day\|schedule_days\|_compute_baseline_power' custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/whatif.py custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/optimizer.py  # callers reached from a coroutine without _await_off_loop

null_control.value: async_simulate(steady=False) (the degree tiles' call): 0 loop simulate_step, 0 ms in schedule_days, heartbeat gap 13.8 ms
null_control.note: the loop calls vanish exactly when schedule_days is not reached

reproduction_steps: Run the command; read <house>.<cell>.loop_simulate_step_calls, .schedule_days_loop_cpu_ms_median and .longest_loop_gap_ms_median, and the perturbed_offloop.* rows.

Leave-one-out over the six steady cells' loop CPU (ms host): dropping the weekend cell (23.9) leaves max 18.5 ms (fuse_cap) = 92.6 ms Pi, under B2: the B2 overrun needs a schedule with more distinct day types, while the loop-side model work itself (384+ calls) is present in every steady cell.
proposed_fix_scope: coordinator.py async_simulate: evaluate both reference_day calls through _await_off_loop (one job returning both) before schedule_days compares them; whatif.schedule_days takes the two (targets, kWh) pairs. A features.py check that a steady what-if makes 0 simulate_step calls on the loop thread.
